title: Traditional Filipino Games
subtitle: Six games, and what each one actually trains.
objectives: Name the main traditional Filipino games
Say which fitness component each one trains
Explain why these games still work as training

cards.title: These games are a training programme nobody wrote down
cards.text: Every one of them trains something specific. Once you can name what, they stop being old games and become drills.

cards.title: Name the component, not the game
cards.text: A game you can name the purpose of is a game you can use.
points: **Agility** — changing direction fast.
**Power** — force produced quickly.
**Balance and coordination** — control under movement.
**Accuracy** — hitting a target under pressure.

cards.title: Six buttons
cards.text: Tap each game. The second line is what it actually trains.

question.explain: Direction changes under pressure, not straight-line speed.

cards.title: Luksong tinik and piko
cards.text: Both involve jumping. They train different things.
points: **Luksong tinik:** a rising stack of hands and feet.
**That is power and flexibility together.**
**Piko:** hopping a grid on one foot.
**That is single-leg balance and ankle control.**

question.explain: Sungka is a counting and strategy game.

cards.title: Sipa is footwork
cards.text: Keeping a weighted shuttle up with your feet is the same skill as not losing your base.
points: **Weight has to stay over your feet.**
**Small corrections, constantly.**
**That is what a boxer's footwork is.**
**Coaches use skipping for the same reason.**

cards.title: Four reasons
cards.text: This is not nostalgia. There are real reasons these games are good training.
points: **No equipment.** A slipper, a can, a stick of chalk.
**Short bursts with rest** — the same shape as interval training.
**Mixed ages can play together**, which keeps it going.
**They are fun**, which is the only reason anyone repeats anything.

cards.title: Short bursts with rest is a real method
cards.text: What these games do by accident, coaches do on purpose.
points: **Sprint, stop, sprint again.**
**That trains the heart differently** from a steady jog.
**It is called interval training.**
**Patintero is intervals** with a reason to run.

cards.title: These games have rules you could code
cards.text: Every one of them is a complete rule set.
points: **Win condition, lose condition, turn order.**
**Tumbang preso has a respawn rule.**
**Patintero has collision detection** — by hand.
**They are games in the strict sense**, not just play.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Patintero: agility. Tumbang preso: accuracy and sprinting.
Sipa: balance and coordination. Luksong tinik: power and flexibility.
Piko: single-leg balance. Sungka: strategy, not fitness.
Short bursts with rest is interval training by another name.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 7 MAPEH, PE strand. The move that makes this week work is refusing the nostalgia framing: each game is labelled with the fitness component it trains, so 'old game' becomes 'specific drill'. Sungka is kept in the set precisely because it trains nothing physical, which forces him to actually read the column rather than assume every traditional game is exercise. The four reasons these games survived are given plainly, including that they are fun, since that is the real mechanism. The gaming lens reframes them as complete rule sets, which they are.
discussion: Ask what each game trains before he plays it.
Ask why sungka is in the list at all.
Ask what interval training is and which game does it.
Ask him to write the rules of patintero as if for a computer.
extension: Play one of these and have him name the component afterwards.
Have him invent a game that trains one named component.
misconceptions: "All traditional games are exercise." Sungka is strategy.
"Patintero is a running race." It is agility, not speed.
"These games are too simple to be training." Short bursts with rest is a real method.
